answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can cap new identities with a verifiable random function lottery: each epoch only a fixed number of registration slots open, drawn unpredictably, so one operator cannot flood the ocean of agents with thousands of sockpuppets at once. Each identity is an island: it must survive a waiting period of honest service before earning full rights, and a violet flag marks identities created in the same draw from the same funding source, letting peers see clusters. Slot scarcity plus public clustering raises the cost of a fake army above its payoff.
